scenario.description: An operations director must decide whether to refurbish a worn stamping die or obtain a replacement for an upcoming production order, and must finalize the downtime and inspection plan with input from maintenance and quality.

shared_context.S1: Stamping die D-18 has visible wear and is needed for an upcoming customer production order.
shared_context.S2: The available options are to refurbish D-18 or obtain a replacement die; Marisol makes the binding decision.
shared_context.S3: A replacement die would require a new tooling order, while refurbishing would use the existing die and take the line out of service.
shared_context.S4: As part of the normal tooling-release process, Marisol asks maintenance and quality to report any relevant findings before authorizing the plan.
shared_context.S5: The tooling-release policy allows Marisol to authorize a refurbishment plan from the maintenance and quality findings; stores confirmation and comparison of an unselected replacement option are follow-up execution matters, not prerequisites for this authorization.

PF1.text: Grant's hands-on inspection found that D-18 can be refurbished by replacing two worn guide inserts, with exactly 10 hours of line downtime; he has not entered the finding in the work-order system because he was waiting for stores to confirm the inserts were available.

PF2.text: Elena's review of the customer's tooling note confirmed that a refurbished D-18 requires a 40-piece first article and dimensional inspection of the first 200 production pieces before release; she completed the review this morning but has not updated the quality plan because document control has not yet posted the note.

acceptance_conditions: D-18 must be refurbished rather than replaced.
The refurbishment plan must reserve exactly 10 hours of line downtime.
The plan must require a 40-piece first article.
The plan must require dimensional inspection of exactly the first 200 production pieces.
The settlement decisions must encode the refurbishment and inspection plan.

decisive_facts.why: The inspection establishes that refurbishment is technically viable and changes the downtime entry to exactly 10 hours instead of authorizing a replacement or leaving the downtime unspecified.
The customer tooling note changes the inspection entries to exactly 40 first-article pieces and exactly 200 production pieces, and requires the customer requirement to be cited.
